description: Larger retrieval evaluation: 66 HR, finance, IT and facilities policies with many near-neighbours (several kinds of leave, overlapping expense rules, two salary band documents, three ways to report misconduct), so a good ranker has to tell similar documents apart. Questions use everyday wording. 'expected' is a title, a list of acceptable titles when more than one document genuinely answers the question, or null when no document does (including tricky questions on neighbouring topics). Questions without a 'slice' are 'general' (everyday paraphrases). The 'exact_terms' slice was added later to judge keyword search fairly: each question uses a term that appears verbatim in the right policy (acronyms like TOIL and VPN, codes like E4 and S3, jargon like tailgating or facilitation payments), plus unanswerable questions naming systems no policy mentions (SAP, Okta, JIRA).

documents.title: Annual leave policy
documents.content:
Full-time employees receive 25 days of paid annual leave per calendar year, in addition to public holidays. Part-time employees receive a pro-rata amount based on their contracted hours.

Requests for absences longer than three days must be submitted in the HRMS at least two weeks in advance. Requests are approved first by your line manager and then by HR.

Up to 5 unused days can be carried over into the first quarter of the following year; any remaining days expire. Untaken days are only paid out when employment ends.

documents.title: Sick leave policy
documents.content:
If you are unwell, notify your manager before 10:00 on the first day of absence. You may self-certify for up to three consecutive working days. From the fourth day of absence a doctor's note is required.

Sick leave is paid at full salary for up to 20 working days per year. Record each absence as sick leave in the HRMS, even if you only record it after you return.

documents.title: Remote work policy
documents.content:
Employees may work from home up to three days per week, as agreed with their manager. Core collaboration hours are 10:00 to 15:00 in your local time zone.

You must use the company VPN and a company-managed laptop when working outside the office.

Working from another country requires HR approval in advance, because of tax and legal implications.

documents.title: Parental leave policy
documents.content:
Birthing parents are entitled to 26 weeks of paid maternity leave. Partners and adoptive parents receive 6 weeks of paid parental leave, which can be taken at any point during the first year.

Notify HR at least 8 weeks before the expected start date. Your role is protected while you are on parental leave.

documents.title: Expense and travel policy
documents.content:
Business expenses must be submitted within 30 days with an itemised receipt. Economy class is standard for flights under six hours; longer flights may be booked in premium economy.

Hotel costs are reimbursed up to 180 per night in major cities. Meals while travelling are covered up to 50 per day. Alcohol is not reimbursed.

Any single expense above 500 needs pre-approval from your manager.

documents.title: IT security policy
documents.content:
Passwords must be at least 14 characters long and must never be reused. Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for email and all internal systems.

Report lost or stolen devices to the IT service desk within one hour. Never share customer data through personal email or messaging apps.

Suspected phishing emails must be reported with the Report button in your mail client.

documents.title: Code of conduct
documents.content:
We expect everyone to treat colleagues, customers and partners with respect. Harassment and discrimination of any kind are not tolerated.

Gifts or hospitality from suppliers worth more than 50 must be declared to the compliance team.

Concerns can be raised confidentially through the whistleblowing hotline, without fear of retaliation.

documents.title: Salary bands
documents.content:
Engineering band E2 pays 70,000 to 90,000 per year. Band E3 (senior engineer) pays 90,000 to 120,000. Band E4 (staff engineer) pays 115,000 to 150,000.

Salaries are reviewed every April based on performance and market data.

documents.title: Learning and development policy
documents.content:
Every employee has an annual learning budget of 1,500 for courses, conferences, books and certifications, and may use up to 5 working days per year for training. Requests are approved by your manager.

If you leave within 12 months of completing a course that cost more than 1,000, you may have to repay part of the cost.

documents.title: Bereavement leave policy
documents.content:
If someone close to you dies, you can take up to 5 days of paid bereavement leave for a partner, child, parent or sibling, and up to 2 days for other relatives or close friends.

The days do not need to be taken in one block and can be used within three months, for example for the funeral. Tell your manager as soon as you can; no documents are needed.

If you need more time, you can add annual leave or unpaid leave, or talk to HR about a phased return.

documents.title: Carer's leave policy
documents.content:
Employees can take up to 3 days of paid carer's leave per year to look after a dependant who is ill, injured or whose care arrangements suddenly break down, such as a child whose nursery closes unexpectedly.

Carer's leave is for emergencies and short-term care. If you need regular time to care for someone, ask about flexible working instead.

Record carer's leave in the HRMS as its own leave type; it does not reduce your annual leave or sick leave.

documents.title: Medical appointments policy
documents.content:
Please book routine doctor, dentist and optician appointments outside core hours where you can. If that is not possible, you can take up to two hours of paid time per appointment without using annual leave.

Antenatal appointments are always paid time off. Hospital stays, operations and recovery count as sick leave, not as medical appointments.

Let your manager know in advance and add the appointment to your calendar.

documents.title: Jury service and civic duties policy
documents.content:
If you are called for jury service, you will receive full pay for up to 10 working days. Send a copy of the court summons to HR as soon as you receive it; HR can ask the court to postpone if the timing is critical for the business.

Time off for other public duties, such as serving as a local councillor, school governor or military reservist, is granted for up to 5 paid days per year.

documents.title: Sabbatical policy
documents.content:
After five years of continuous service you can apply for a sabbatical of one to three months. Sabbaticals are unpaid, and your benefits are paused while you are away, but your job is kept for you.

Apply through the HRMS at least six months before you want to start. Requests are approved by your manager and the head of your department, taking business needs into account.

documents.title: Unpaid leave policy
documents.content:
You can request up to 20 days of unpaid leave per year for personal reasons that annual leave does not cover. Unpaid leave needs approval from both your manager and HR.

Unpaid leave reduces your salary for the month in which it is taken, and pension contributions are reduced accordingly. You must normally use your remaining annual leave first.

documents.title: Public holidays policy
documents.content:
Each December, HR publishes the public holiday calendar for every country where we have an office. Public holidays are in addition to your 25 days of annual leave.

If you are asked to work on a public holiday, you receive a day off in lieu, to be taken within two months. Part-time employees receive public holidays pro rata.

documents.title: Time off in lieu policy
documents.content:
If your manager asks you in advance to work extra hours, for example during a release weekend, you earn time off in lieu (TOIL) hour for hour.

TOIL must be recorded in the HRMS within one week and used within three months; it expires after that and cannot be paid out. Extra hours that were not agreed in advance do not earn TOIL.

documents.title: Religious observance policy
documents.content:
We support employees who need time for religious festivals and observance. You can use annual leave or unpaid leave for religious holidays, and you may swap a public holiday for another day of religious significance with your manager's agreement.

A quiet room for prayer and reflection is available on the third floor of each office.

documents.title: Exam leave policy
documents.content:
For job-related qualifications that the company has agreed to support, you get one day of paid exam leave for each exam, plus the day before the exam for revision.

Exam leave is separate from the training days in the learning and development policy. Book it in the HRMS and attach the exam confirmation.

documents.title: Mileage and car use policy
documents.content:
If you use your own car for business journeys, you can claim 0.30 per kilometre for the extra distance beyond your normal commute. Your normal commute to the office is never reimbursed.

Your car insurance must cover business use. Parking fees and tolls on business journeys can be claimed with receipts; parking fines and speeding tickets cannot.

documents.title: Corporate card policy
documents.content:
Employees who travel more than four times a year can request a corporate credit card. The card is for business expenses only; personal purchases are not allowed, even if you pay them back.

Card transactions must be matched with receipts in the expense tool by the 5th of the following month. If the card is lost or stolen, call the bank's emergency number and inform finance on the same day.

documents.title: Client entertainment policy
documents.content:
Entertaining clients is allowed when there is a clear business purpose. The limit is 75 per person, and events with more than six guests need approval from your manager in advance.

Record the names of all attendees and the purpose of the meeting with the expense claim. As with other expenses, alcohol is not reimbursed.

documents.title: International travel policy
documents.content:
All business trips abroad are covered by the company travel insurance; you do not need to buy your own. Register every international trip in the travel portal before you go so that we can contact you in an emergency.

Check visa requirements at least six weeks before travelling; HR can provide invitation letters. Trips to countries rated high-risk require approval from the security team.

documents.title: Travel booking policy
documents.content:
Book all flights, trains and hotels through the company travel portal, at least 14 days in advance where possible. For journeys under four hours, take the train rather than flying.

Loyalty points and air miles earned on business travel are yours to keep, but they must not influence which airline or hotel you choose.

documents.title: Relocation policy
documents.content:
When the company asks you to move to another city or country for your role, we pay removal costs up to 8,000 and up to 30 days of temporary accommodation. We also cover one house-hunting trip.

If you resign within 12 months of relocating, you must repay a share of the relocation costs.

documents.title: Acceptable use policy
documents.content:
Company laptops, phones and accounts are for work. Limited personal use, such as checking the news at lunch, is fine as long as it does not affect your work or break the law.

Never use company systems to access illegal or offensive content. We monitor network traffic for security purposes, in line with data protection law.

documents.title: Bring your own device policy
documents.content:
You may read work email and chat on your personal phone, but only through the company's mobile app after enrolling the device with IT. The phone must have a screen lock and an up-to-date operating system.

If a personal phone that has work data on it is lost or stolen, report it to the IT service desk within one hour; IT can remotely wipe the work profile without touching your personal data.

documents.title: Software installation policy
documents.content:
Only install software from the company software catalogue. If you need a tool that is not in the catalogue, request it in the IT portal; a security review usually takes five working days.

Browser extensions count as software. Unlicensed or pirated software is never allowed.

documents.title: Data classification policy
documents.content:
Company information has four levels: public, internal, confidential and restricted. Customer personal data and salary information are restricted.

Restricted data may only be stored in approved systems, never on USB drives or personal cloud storage, and must be encrypted when sent outside the company.

documents.title: Laptop and IT equipment policy
documents.content:
Laptops are replaced every three years. If your laptop is broken or too slow for your work, request a replacement or repair through the IT portal.

Never take company equipment to a third-party repair shop. Monitors, keyboards and headsets for the office can be ordered from the IT catalogue.

documents.title: Home office equipment policy
documents.content:
Employees who work from home at least two days per week can claim a one-off allowance of 400 for home office furniture, such as a desk or an ergonomic chair. Submit the receipts within three months of purchase.

The company also lends you a monitor and a docking station, which must be returned when you leave.

documents.title: Internet and phone costs policy
documents.content:
If you work from home regularly, the company reimburses up to 30 per month towards your home internet bill. Claim it quarterly through the expense tool.

Employees who are on call receive a company mobile phone. Other employees can claim business calls made on a personal phone if they exceed 20 per month.

documents.title: Working abroad policy
documents.content:
You can work from another country for up to 20 working days per year, but only from countries on the approved list, and only with HR approval obtained before you travel.

Longer stays can create tax and social security obligations for you and the company, so they are not allowed. Working from sanctioned countries is never permitted.

documents.title: Coworking space policy
documents.content:
Employees who live more than 50 kilometres from the nearest office can ask the company to pay for a coworking space membership of up to 150 per month.

The space must be booked through the travel portal provider so that the invoice goes directly to the company.

documents.title: Flexible working policy
documents.content:
After 26 weeks of employment, anyone can request flexible working, such as different start and finish times, a compressed four-day week or part-time hours.

Submit the request in the HRMS. Your manager must reply within one month, and a request can only be refused for a business reason, which will be explained to you.

documents.title: Payroll and pay dates
documents.content:
Salaries are paid on the 25th of each month. If the 25th falls on a weekend or public holiday, you are paid on the previous working day.

Your payslip is available in the HRMS two days before payday. Questions about your pay should go to the payroll team through the HR portal.

documents.title: Bonus scheme
documents.content:
Most employees are eligible for an annual bonus of up to 10% of base salary. The amount depends on company results and your individual performance rating.

Bonuses are paid with the March salary. You must still be employed, and not under notice, on the payment date to receive it.

documents.title: Overtime policy
documents.content:
Employees in bands E1, E2 and S1 are paid 1.5 times their hourly rate for overtime that their manager approved in advance. More senior employees are not paid for overtime; they can earn time off in lieu instead.

Overtime is recorded in the HRMS and paid with the following month's salary.

documents.title: Pension scheme
documents.content:
You are automatically enrolled in the company pension scheme after one month. If you contribute at least 4% of your salary, the company contributes 6%.

You can change your contribution or opt out at any time through the pension provider's website. Opting out means you lose the company contribution.

documents.title: Sales salary bands
documents.content:
Sales band S1 (account executive) pays 50,000 to 65,000 per year, band S2 (senior account executive) pays 65,000 to 85,000, and band S3 (sales manager) pays 85,000 to 110,000.

Sales roles also earn commission of up to 40% of base salary, paid quarterly.

documents.title: Stock option plan
documents.content:
Selected roles receive stock options when they join. Options vest over four years, with the first 25% vesting after one year (the cliff) and the rest monthly after that.

If you leave, you have 90 days to exercise vested options. Unvested options are cancelled.

documents.title: Private health insurance
documents.content:
All employees are covered by private medical insurance from their first day, and can add a partner and children free of charge. Dental cover is optional and costs 12 per month.

Claims are made through the insurer's app. Pre-existing conditions are covered after two years of membership.

documents.title: Employee assistance programme
documents.content:
Our employee assistance programme offers free, confidential counselling by phone or video, available 24 hours a day. You can have up to six sessions per issue.

It also offers legal and financial advice, for example on debt or housing problems. Nothing you discuss is shared with the company.

documents.title: Cycle to work and commuting
documents.content:
Through the cycle to work scheme you can get a bike and equipment worth up to 1,500, paid through your salary before tax over 12 months.

We also offer an interest-free loan for annual public transport season tickets, repaid from your salary over 10 months.

documents.title: Wellbeing allowance
documents.content:
Every employee receives a wellbeing allowance of 40 per month, which can be spent on gym memberships, fitness classes, sports clubs or wellbeing apps.

Claim it through the benefits platform with a receipt. Unused allowance does not roll over to the next month.

documents.title: Life and income protection insurance
documents.content:
All employees have life insurance worth four times their annual salary from their first day. Tell HR who should receive the payment by filling in the nomination form.

If you cannot work because of long-term illness or injury, income protection insurance pays 75% of your salary after 26 weeks of absence, until you can return or retire.

documents.title: On-call allowance
documents.content:
Engineers on the on-call rota receive 150 for each week on call, plus overtime or time off in lieu for any hours spent handling incidents outside normal working hours.

You must be able to respond within 15 minutes while on call. Swaps between colleagues are allowed if the rota is updated.

documents.title: Conflicts of interest policy
documents.content:
Declare any situation where your personal interests could conflict with the company's, for example a second job, a side business, a family member working for a supplier, or shares in a competitor.

Declarations are made in the compliance portal and reviewed by your manager. Side projects that use company time, equipment or information are not allowed.

documents.title: Anti-bribery policy
documents.content:
Never offer, give or accept a bribe, including small 'facilitation payments' to speed up routine government services.

All gifts and hospitality you give or receive, whatever their value, must be recorded in the gifts register. Gifts worth more than 50 also need approval from the compliance team before you accept them.

documents.title: Social media policy
documents.content:
You may say where you work on social media, but make clear that your views are your own. Never share confidential information, customer details or unreleased products.

If a journalist contacts you, do not reply yourself; forward the request to the communications team.

documents.title: Anti-harassment and bullying procedure
documents.content:
If you experience or witness harassment or bullying, you can raise it with your manager, with HR, or anonymously through the whistleblowing hotline.

HR will start an investigation within 10 working days and keep you informed. You can bring a colleague to any meeting, and support is available through the employee assistance programme.

documents.title: Whistleblowing policy
documents.content:
Report suspected fraud, corruption, safety risks or breaches of law through the whistleblowing hotline, which is run by an independent provider and can be used anonymously by phone or online.

You are protected from any retaliation for reporting a genuine concern, even if it turns out to be unfounded.

documents.title: Relationships at work policy
documents.content:
Romantic or family relationships between colleagues are a private matter, unless one person has authority over the other, for example as their manager.

In that case, both people must tell HR so that reporting lines or approval rights can be changed. You will not be penalised for disclosing a relationship.

documents.title: Data protection policy
documents.content:
Only collect the personal data you need and keep it only as long as necessary. If someone asks for a copy of their personal data, forward the request to the privacy team immediately; we must answer within 30 days.

Suspected data breaches, such as an email sent to the wrong person, must be reported to the privacy team within 24 hours.

documents.title: Probation policy
documents.content:
New employees have a six-month probation period, with review meetings after three and six months. Your manager can extend probation by up to three months if more time is needed.

During probation either side can end the employment with one week's notice.

documents.title: Resignation and notice periods
documents.content:
After probation, the notice period is one month for most employees and three months for managers. Resign in writing through the HRMS; your manager and HR will confirm your last working day.

The company may ask you not to come to work during your notice period (garden leave), in which case you are still paid.

documents.title: Offboarding policy
documents.content:
On your last day, return your laptop, phone, badge and any other company equipment to IT or reception. Your accounts are disabled at 18:00 on your last working day.

Any annual leave you have not taken is paid with your final salary. You will be invited to an optional exit interview with HR.

documents.title: References policy
documents.content:
Only HR may give employment references on behalf of the company. A reference confirms your job title and dates of employment.

Managers may give personal references only if they make clear that they are not speaking for the company. Requests from future employers should be forwarded to HR.

documents.title: Internal mobility policy
documents.content:
You can apply for open internal roles after 12 months in your current role. Internal vacancies are posted on the careers page of the intranet one week before they are advertised externally.

Tell your manager before your final interview. Internal moves usually take effect after one month.

documents.title: Performance review policy
documents.content:
Performance reviews take place twice a year, in June and December. You write a self-assessment, your manager adds feedback from colleagues, and you receive a rating from 1 to 5.

Ratings affect your bonus and promotion chances. If you disagree with your rating, you can ask your manager's manager for a second review within 10 days.

documents.title: Promotion policy
documents.content:
Promotions are decided twice a year at the calibration meetings after the June and December reviews. Your manager nominates you with examples of work at the next level.

If you are promoted, your new band and salary apply from the first day of the following month.

documents.title: Mentoring programme
documents.content:
Anyone can join the mentoring programme as a mentee or mentor. Sign up in the HRMS and you will be matched with someone from another team within a month.

Mentoring pairs usually meet once a month for six months. Conversations are confidential.

documents.title: Fire safety policy
documents.content:
The fire alarm is tested every Wednesday at 10:00; at any other time, leave the building immediately by the nearest exit. Do not use the lifts.

The assembly point is car park B, where fire wardens in yellow vests will take a head count.

documents.title: Accident reporting policy
documents.content:
Report every accident, injury or near miss at work in the HRMS within 24 hours, even if nobody was hurt. Names of trained first aiders are posted next to each kitchen.

If you are injured while working from home during working hours, report it in the same way.

documents.title: Workstation ergonomics policy
documents.content:
Everyone who works at a screen can request a workstation assessment from the facilities team, at the office or at home. Adjustable chairs, footrests and laptop stands are available on request.

The company reimburses an eye test every two years, and up to 60 towards glasses needed for screen work.

documents.title: Office access and visitors policy
documents.content:
Always wear your badge in the office. Do not let people follow you through a secure door without badging in (tailgating).

Visitors must be registered in advance, signed in at reception and accompanied at all times. Lost badges must be reported to security immediately so they can be deactivated.
